sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the tests
sections.what: Brings in the testing tools, the consent service, and the database access piece it depends on.
sections.why: Likely reason: each test file loads what it touches.

sections.name: ConsentService (DPDP Compliance) (part 1)
sections.title: Fake database and first grant test
sections.what: Creates a fake database with consent and audit stubs, builds the testing module, and checks that granting a consent for the first time creates a new record and returns it as granted.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the basic grant path works when no earlier record exists.

sections.name: ConsentService (DPDP Compliance) (part 2)
sections.title: Re-grant test
sections.what: Checks that granting consent again on a withdrawn record updates the same record to granted, clears its withdrawal time, and does not create a duplicate. Also checks that the audit entry for granting is written.
sections.why: Likely reason: users may grant, withdraw and re-grant, so each re-grant must reuse the same record for a clear history.
sections.watch_out: The test checks the audit entry for the first grant only in the visible part, so the re-grant audit is not confirmed here.

sections.name: ConsentService (DPDP Compliance) (part 3)
sections.title: Tests for withdrawing and checking consent
sections.what: Checks that withdrawing consent marks the stored record as not granted, writes a CONSENT_REVOKED audit entry, and returns the updated record. Also checks that a purpose with an active grant returns true and a withdrawn grant returns false.
sections.why: Likely reason: withdrawing consent is a legal right, so the revoke path and the yes or no check are protected by tests.
sections.watch_out: The withdrawal test checks that the update sets isGranted to false but does not check the withdrawal timestamp.

sections.name: ConsentService (DPDP Compliance) (part 4)
sections.title: Test for a purpose with no record
sections.what: Finishes the consent check tests by confirming that a purpose with no stored record returns false. This closes the test group.
sections.why: Likely reason: a missing record must never be read as permission to use data.

summary: Automated checks that granting a consent creates a new record or turns a withdrawn one back on, and writes an audit entry.
purpose: Protects the consent granting behaviour, which the chat feature relies on through the consent check.
why: Likely reason: consent records are legal proof, so their behaviour is tested. Fake database calls keep the tests fast.
how: 1. Builds a fake database with consent and audit functions. 2. Creates the testing module with the real service. 3. Tests granting a new consent. 4. Tests re-granting a withdrawn consent.
inputs: No outside input. Each test sets the fake results it needs.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: Only the granting behaviour is visible here. Revoking, listing and status checks are not shown in this packet. Fake calls may not match the real database.
debug: Run the Jest test for this file. Read the failing expectation. Check that stubs match any new database calls in the service.
